title: Feedback Indicators: The Alignment between Llama and a Teacher in Language Learning
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how well large language model (LLM)–generated feedback indicators align with human teacher ratings in a foreign-language learning context. The authors frame the problem as one of making automated formative feedback more transparent and explainable by first extracting interpretable indicators from student texts, rather than directly asking the model to score submissions end-to-end.

The intervention/approach studied is an indicator-extraction pipeline using Llama 3.1. The model is prompted with binary and list-style queries to identify textual indicators such as form of address, sociolinguistic appropriateness, vocabulary use, coherence, grammar, and related features from student submissions. These indicator values are then compared with teacher ratings from an established rubric through correlation analysis.

The study took place in an online French-as-a-foreign-language course at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. The participants were 22 university students enrolled in a B1-level course; 11 students submitted the analyzed task and consented to the use of their submissions. Teacher feedback was given using a Moodle rubric with 10 criteria, and the paper examines whether LLM-extracted indicators can serve as useful proxies for those criteria.

The main conclusion is that many extracted indicators showed moderate to strong correlations with at least one teacher-rated criterion, suggesting that LLMs can support a transparent feedback pipeline. However, the alignment between the intended indicator and criterion was often weaker than expected, indicating that high-level feedback criteria are complex and may be captured indirectly by different textual features. The authors argue that their approach could support teacher-assistive automated feedback and also help reveal which indicators teachers implicitly use when grading.

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: A family of open-weight large language models developed by Meta for text generation and other language tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the LLM to extract binary and list-based feedback indicators from students’ French language submissions and compare those extracted indicators with teacher ratings on a rubric.

findings.finding_summary: In an online French-as-a-foreign-language course (level B1), Llama 3.1-generated indicators showed statistically significant moderate-to-high alignment with teacher ratings across multiple rubric criteria. The paper reports that 44 of 63 extracted indicators (70%) had acceptable correlations with at least one criterion (|PCC|  .5), and 15 indicators had high correlations (|PCC|  .70); the study involved 11 consenting students who completed the analyzed task.
findings.measure: Pearson correlation between LLM-extracted feedback indicators and teacher ratings on feedback criteria

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single correlational study rather than an experimental impact evaluation. The paper provides quantitative alignment evidence, but not causal evidence of learning gains or teacher performance improvements.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effect is promising but indirect: correlations between extracted indicators and teacher ratings, not student outcome gains. The study suggests moderate to high alignment, but impact on instruction or learning is not established.
